response.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT pc.college_id, COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(co.state),''),'') AS state, COUNT(DISTINCT pc.player_id) AS cnt FROM player_college pc JOIN college co ON co.college_id = pc.college_id GROUP BY pc.college_id, COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(co.state),''),'')) SELECT state, AVG(cnt*1.0) AS avg_count, AVG(cnt*1.0/(SELECT AVG(cnt*1.0) FROM c)) AS avg_ratio_to_overall_avg, AVG(cnt*1.0/(SELECT SUM(cnt) FROM c)) AS avg_share_of_total FROM c GROUP BY state

assumptions.assumption: NULL, empty and whitespace-only states are merged into one group (shown as an empty string).
college_id is unique in college, so each matched college appears once. The overall average and total are taken over all matched colleges, not per state.
Counts are cast to decimals (x*1.0) to avoid integer division, and nothing is rounded.
